mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% over three months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the rank IC drops below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when unemployment is simultaneously falling.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate margins, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered months, or the effect reverses when wage growth (not observed) is accelerating.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which tends to precede negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days due to lower earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered periods, or the effect disappears during periods of strong commodity price inflation (not observed).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above their respective 5-year averages signals a stagflationary environment, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days due to higher discount rates and eroded real earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when oil prices (not observed) are collapsing.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 10-year moving average for three consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to construction sector and consumer confidence spillovers.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 10-year MA for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during periods of rising mortgage rates (not observed).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE (i.e., more people working but unemployment rising due to labor force expansion) over two months signals demographic-driven labor market expansion rather than cyclical improvement, which historically has been neutral to slightly positive for S&P 500 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0% MoM AND UNRATE > 0% MoM for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during periods of falling real wages (not observed).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in Real Savings (RSAFS) below its 5-year average for six consecutive months signals reduced household savings and higher consumption, which typically boosts corporate earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 5-year average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect disappears during periods of extreme fiscal tightening (not observed).
